mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the same period are not statistically lower than during the prior 60-day period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rates (UNRATE) accompanied by a decline in payrolls (PAYEMS) indicate weakening labor market conditions, which typically precede S&P 500 declines over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4% while PAYEMS declines over the next month
failure_condition: A 5-day moving average of 20-day forward returns remains positive during the labor cooling phase (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) during a period of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 305) suggests strong demand that supports equity valuations, driving positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 for three consecutive months, despite falling unemployment, signals supply-side weakness that depresses equity valuations and produces negative 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive in all INDPRO contraction phases (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 4%, the discount rate for future cash flows rises, reducing expected equity valuations and generating negative 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p-value > 0.05) during the tightening normalization phase.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (not directly observable in the provided catalog but implied by labor dynamics) coinciding with a sharp drop in unemployment (UNRATE) triggers optimism about labor market recovery, pushing 20-day forward returns positive in regime 'recovery acceleration'.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE drops by 0.5 percentage points in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative during the recovery acceleration phase (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of double-digit GDP deflator (implied by CPIAUCSL > 310) without a corresponding rise in industrial production (INDPRO) suggest demand-driven inflation, which is associated with negative 60-day forward returns as investors fear future rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL exceeds 310 for two consecutive months while INDPRO remains flat or declining
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than during the prior inflationary period (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in S&P 500 total returns is positive but the 12-month change in dividend yield is also positive, indicating a shift from capital appreciation to income-driven returns, the next 20-day forward returns tend to be negative due to mean-reversion in equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive during the valuation mean-reversion episode (p-value > 0.05).
